title: Revise a project memory in place: an attributed revision of a stable key keeps prior versions as history and serves the current body through the original key
outcome: Revise a project memory in place: an attributed revision of a stable key keeps prior versions as history and serves the current body through the original key
acceptance: A project memory revised at least twice survives graph snapshot save and load into an empty store with every attributed version, author and order retained and the current version current; malformed or out-of-order history refuses atomically without partial import
After two revisions and forget, snapshot export and load preserve only the retirement and no body from any version; origin retains canonical history locally while all full reads remain retired

CLI and MCP agree; docs state the revision model in one paragraph (current body by key, history retained, forget retires permanently) and remove any suggestion to fragment a rule across companion keys

a revise against a key whose current version differs from the caller's expected basis refuses with a typed conflict naming the current version instead of silently overwriting; an identical retry of the same revision replays without a duplicate version; remember on an existing key without --revise still refuses memory_exists and its receipt offers the revise path; a retired (forgotten) key still refuses ProjectMemoryRetired

engram work remember TEXT --key KEY --revise (MCP remember with revise: true) records an attributed new version of an existing live key; the revised body is what memories KEY, memories --after and ordinary retrieval return through the original key; the previous body and its attribution stay retrievable as history (memories KEY --full or a versions view), never rewritten

completion.summary: Stable-key attributed memory revisions, historical reads, strict optional CAS and replay, terminal retirement, and snapshot history retention delivered in 22ffb93.
